metrics.outcome: Stopped: every done-when item passes with Audit's evidence, but Identity did not declare done. Done means the done-when list only, so this needs a look at Identity's reason above.
metrics.brief: A one-page website for Brew Lab, a small specialty coffee shop in Indiranagar, Bengaluru. Visitors should see the menu with prices, the opening hours, and where to find us, and be able to pre-order a coffee for pickup. It should feel warm and modern and work well on a phone. Include a section about our beans and the farms they come from, and a simple loyalty-card explainer (buy 9, get the 10th free).

estimate_vs_charged.name: Page shell, anchor nav and warm mobile-first styling
Menu, opening hours and where-to-find-us sections
Pickup pre-order form with order summary

open_inputs: Menu items and prices in INR
Phone, WhatsApp or email for contact
How pre-orders reach the shop (WhatsApp number, email or other) and whether payment is at pickup or online
Pickup time rules (earliest slot, lead time)
Bean names, roast details, and the farms and regions they come from

review.verdict: The department built all ten done-when items in one cycle for 90 of 200 budget, but shipped a 10px overflow at 360px, and the run stopped before the rework Identity ordered could happen.

identity.note: The charter [2] was sound, with no invented facts. The ruling at [24] cites the 360px no-scroll standard, which is a defensible reading of 'material finding'. But it blocked 'done' on a clause that is not in done-when, so it effectively widened done-when (openly, not silently). It also mentioned the 8-cost fix, which drifts toward Priority's territory.

adaptation.note: One turn, one proposal [4]: four small workflows, 90 of 200, unknowns marked as placeholders. Efficient and in role. It never got to act on the rework, and I can't see its completion checks, so evidence is thin.

priority.note: It granted all four with envelopes tied to done-when items and left 110 in reserve for fixes [5]. It named an 8 price for a fix, and Identity used that figure. It did not push back on the four-way split. 'None is padded' is asserted, not shown.

coordination.note: It stated its scheduling rule every time, gave exact HOLD conditions [10][14], and kept one writer on index.html. One claim was wrong: [7] promised each handoff would be 'Audit-clean', but Audit ran only once, at the end.

audit.note: It used the code measurement and said plainly that it could not find the cause [22]. 'Please fix it and re-run' edges into repair and scheduling, which the role forbids. The overflow-x:hidden cause is a guess, though marked 'may'. Its prose says 9 of 10 pass, but the code counts all_pass true.

builder.note: It stayed in scope on each of four runs and reported untouched stubs [13][19]. Result: 30 KB, no JS errors, no broken links, every unknown marked as a placeholder. It shipped a phone overflow on a brief that stresses phones. The cause is unknown.

went_well: Clean run: 0 invalid moves, 0 validator refusals, 13 AI calls, 5.8 minutes, 90 of 200 spent.
Placeholders were respected: 6 menu rows with placeholder names and prices [13], 'not sent' on the order summary [16], and the exact loyalty line [19].
The single-writer lock serialized W-1 to W-4 without collisions, and HOLD released budget back [11].
The code overflow measurement [21] gave Audit a hard fact to cite.
problems: The 360px no-scroll rule is in standards but not in done-when. Done-when item 8 only checks the viewport meta tag and responsive CSS. So the harness reads 'all pass' while Identity reads 'not done' [24], and the run ends with no rework.

The route check at [23] sent Audit's pick of Adaptation to Identity because 'everything passes'. team.md allows Audit to Adaptation for correctable defects, and F-11 was NEEDS_REVISION. The code's all_pass ignored that finding.
The mechanical check ran only on v4, so there is no way to tell which workflow introduced the overflow. A guess is the W-4 loyalty graphic, unverified.
The Requester was asked nothing about 8 open inputs. This is allowed by the charter, but the page is a template, with no real menu, hours or address.
The envelope estimates equal the charges exactly (rate card). Budget data says nothing about estimation accuracy.
learnings: Put 'no horizontal scroll at 360px' into done-when, or state that standards count toward done. Evidence: [24] and the outcome line.
Compute all_pass from findings (any NEEDS_REVISION means not pass) and allow Audit to Adaptation on those. Evidence: [22][23] and metrics.
Continue the cycle after Identity rules for rework. Otherwise this test cannot show whether the 8-cost fix works. Next test: rerun from v4 with the rework allowed.
Run the code mechanical check after every workflow, not only at the end. It is cheap and would pin the defect to one run.
Keep the one-proposal, serial, rate-card setup. Test next: a brief with real menu and hours, to see how agents treat supplied facts.
Evidence is thin: one cycle, one model, one brief. It does not show whether rework or Requester questions work.
